Diagnosis:
The current bug report states that StringUtils.join throws a NullPointerException (NPE) when the toString method of one of the objects in the array returns null. The example given uses an anonymous object where toString returns null. 

The test case provided calls StringUtils.join on some object array NULL_TO_STRING_LIST. The test expects the join method to produce the string "null" rather than throw an exception.

Looking at the join implementation with signature join(Object[], String, int, int), this method does the join by iterating over the array elements between startIndex and endIndex, appending the separator then appending the element. The relevant snippet is:

```java
if (array[i] != null) {
    buf.append(array[i]);  // relies on toString()
}
```

The StringBuilder.append(Object) internally calls toString on the object. If that toString returns null, StringBuilder.append will throw a NullPointerException.

Also in the initialization of the StringBuilder, we see:

```java
new StringBuilder((array[startIndex] == null ? 16 : array[startIndex].toString().length()) + separator.length());
```

Here again, array[startIndex].toString() is called without null safety checks. If toString returns null here, the call to length() on that result will also throw NullPointerException.

Therefore, the root cause is that the join implementation assumes that the toString method of the objects never returns null (it may handle null objects in the array but not null strings returned from toString). The contract was never explicit but apparently some implementations (e.g., javax.mail.internet.InternetAddress) can break this by returning null from toString.

The test fails because the join method throws a NullPointerException instead of safely handling the null string result from toString. The implementation needs to be defensive: any null resulting from toString should be replaced by the literal "null" string to avoid NPE and to produce meaningful output.

Recent bug reports from the retrieval are unrelated based on their summaries and descriptions and do not contribute relevant information.

Summary: The bug arises because StringUtils.join does not check for null results from the toString of array elements. This causes an NPE when length() called on that null string or when StringBuilder.append tries to append null. The fix is to handle null toString results safely by replacing them with the string "null".

Next, I will identify the best methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.join(java.lang.Object[], java.lang.String, int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
